basis: Recurrent oral mucosal ulceration is an immune-mediated inflammatory disease, despite its unknown initiating cause.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: recurrent aphthous stomatitis has a recognized immune-mediated mucosal injury mechanism; an unknown trigger does not exclude this axis.

basis: Hepatic heme-synthesis disorder; motor polyneuropathy and blistering skin erosions each occur in 30-79%. Abdominal pain alone does not establish GI damage.

decisions.hepatic: primary: explicitly an acute hepatic porphyria, located in hepatic heme synthesis; primary location does not require frequent liver injury.

basis: Developmental delay in 2/3 and congenital diaphragmatic muscle defects in 3/5 characterize the syndrome. Individual cardiac and renal anomalies occur in 1/5.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: congenital diaphragmatic hernia in 3/5 is a major defining structural muscle defect in this deletion syndrome.

basis: Lentigines and cardiac disease define it; ptosis occurs in 8/9 and structural pectus deformities in about 50% or more. Hearing loss usually remains below 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: pectus carinatum/excavatum and other structural skeletal abnormalities affect about half or more of patients with Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines.

basis: Dermal defects and distichiasis (19/21) define it; sacroiliac anomalies occur in 80-99%, anal atresia in 2/3 assessed. Urinary anomalies (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: none: upper urinary tract anomalies occur in 30-79%, but are omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of more frequent skeletal anomalies and severe anorectal defects.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: structural sacroiliac joint abnormalities are reported in 80-99%, supporting common skeletal involvement.

basis: Destructive mast-cell malignancy; reported series describe bone involvement in ~78% and gastrointestinal involvement in ~35%. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: direct gastrointestinal tumor involvement is reported in approximately 35% of cases, meeting the threshold for occupation by the malignancy.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: destructive osseous tumor involvement is reported in approximately 78% of cases.

basis: Meningeal tumor of the sellar diaphragm; optic apparatus compression causes visual impairment in most symptomatic series (>50%). Common pituitary dysfunction is not established.

decisions.ocular: involved: direct optic apparatus compression with visual impairment occurs in most clinical series (>50%), exceeding the threshold.

basis: Axonal peripheral neuropathy with congenital ptosis and early cataracts explicitly defining this subtype. Occasional neutropenia is excluded.

decisions.ocular: primary: congenital ptosis and early cataract are explicitly part of this subtype's defining phenotype, rather than incidental complications.

basis: Optic atrophy 3/3; pancreatic insufficiency and urethral valve each reported once among three cases (~33%; uncertain). ASD and arthrogryposis omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: involved: posterior urethral valve is a structural obstructive urinary defect reported once among three cases (~33%); frequency evidence is sparse.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: exocrine pancreatic insufficiency establishes direct functional loss, reported once among three cases (~33%); frequency evidence is sparse.

basis: CID with defining lymphopenia/neutropenia; bronchiectasis 3/4 and atrial septal defect 2/3. Skin infections are separately diagnosed infections.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital structural heart disease is part of the syndrome; secundum atrial septal defect occurs in 2/3 assessed patients.
decisions.dermatologic: none: warts, candidiasis and skin abscesses are separate infections enabled by immunodeficiency, rather than direct skin injury from STK4 deficiency.
